profiles.name: WhiskeyRich
profiles.profile: This is the kind of card that makes a man stare at a 30-putt line and ask who exactly got paid in this operation. The ball was at least showing up to class around the greens, but the flatstick absolutely torched the place and dragged the whole round into the ditch. Four greens is a rough way to live, but the real crime scene is how quickly a few saveable holes turned into a parade of doubles and dead hope.

profiles.name: jamescripps06
profiles.tagline: SHORT GAME IN A KNIFE FIGHT
profiles.profile: The weird part here is that the long stuff has enough teeth to keep the ceiling alive, but the scoring tools around it are absolutely mugging the round. When the putter and touch game both go missing, all those decent approach numbers just become expensive window dressing. This profile is basically: can find greens, then immediately set the greens on fire. Volatile, messy, and very much a case of the scorecard being bullied by the wedges and the putter.

profiles.name: Bradford
profiles.tagline: ELITE IRONS, EVERY OTHER DEPARTMENT SUSPECT
profiles.profile: This is the classic golf crime: the approach play is screaming, the gross side looks legit, and the net result still comes out like the clubhead was haunted. The ball-striking is loud enough to make you think a breakout is coming any minute, but the rest of the bag keeps turning good field position into a very avoidable tax bill. If the short game ever decides to stop being dramatic, this thing gets dangerous fast. Until then, it’s a lot of pretty shots followed by a lot of annoyed math.

profiles.name: Friendboy
profiles.profile: Friendboy’s card has a strange little split personality: enough touch to keep the round from fully face-planting, but not enough clean contact to stop the bogey drip. The putter has been the best employee in the building, and that’s usually a sign the rest of the bag has been clocking in late. There’s some decent short-game life here, but it keeps getting forced to clean up after a tee-to-green setup that never really gets organized. Functional, scrappy, and always one bad stretch away from looking way worse.

profiles.name: Jonty
profiles.tagline: BALL-STRIKING WITH A SIDE OF CHAOS
profiles.profile: The gross golf is clearly the loudest thing in the room here, and the weird part is the card still finds ways to wobble around the edges. The irons are cooking, the scoring chances are real, and then the round occasionally trips over its own feet with too many putts and some self-inflicted mess. This is not a tidy profile; it’s a guy who can absolutely stripe it and still leave you muttering into the cart cupholder. Dangerous upside, but also enough chaos to keep the stress level spiked.

profiles.name: tburke
profiles.profile: This one is pretty simple: not enough clean stuff, too much scrambling from the wrong side of the ledger, and the whole thing bogged down by a putter that never really bailed anybody out. When you’re living on that many bogeys, the round stops feeling like golf and starts feeling like paperwork. There’s not a ton of mystery here yet — the card needs more help at basically every checkpoint. Right now it’s less ‘grind’ and more ‘slow leak with receipts’.
